title: Equip Me for the War
description: Equip Me for the War in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 270. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-quip me for the war, And teach my hands to fight, My sim-ple, up-right heart pre_-pare, And guide my words a-right; Con-trol my ev-ery thought, My whole of sin re-move; Let all my works in thee be wrought, Let all be wrought in love.

lines: And teach my hands to fight,
Let all my works in thee be wrought,
Let all be wrought in love.
O arm me with the mind,
Meek Lamb! which was in thee,
And let my knowing zeal be joined
O do not let me trust
Humble, O humble to the dust
The help which upon earth is wrought,
O may I love like thee!
O may I learn the art
To hate the sin with all my heart,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
